articles.title: Lucélia Albuquerque, fundadora do Guerreiros do Passo, morre no Recife | G1
articles.standfirst: Coletivo recifense ganhou fama internacional ao desfilar em Cannes com elenco de 'O Agente Secreto', em 2025. Dançarina lutava contra câncer na medula havia sete anos.
articles.summary: Dançarina tinha 44 anos e lutava contra câncer na medula havia sete anos. Grupo ganhou fama internacional ao desfilar em Cannes com elenco de 'O Agente Secreto'.
articles.body:
Morreu no Recife , na madrugada deste domingo (8) a professora e passista de frevo Lucélia Albuquerque, uma das fundadoras do Guerreiros do Passo, grupo de frevo que se tornou Patrimônio Cultural do Recife e ganhou fama internacional ao desfilar no Festival de Cannes com o elenco do filme "O Agente Secreto" (veja vídeo acima) .

Segundo a família, a morte de Lucélia foi confirmada por volta da 1h20. Ela tinha 44 anos e fazia tratamento havia sete anos contra o mieloma múltiplo, um tipo de câncer que se origina na medula óssea. O velório é realizado na Casa Batista, no bairro de Santo Amaro, no Centro do Recife. O enterro está marcado para as 15h, no Cemitério de Santo Amaro.

Ao g1 , o viúvo de Lucélia e também fundador do grupo, Eduardo Araújo, contou que ela estava internada desde o dia 30 de outubro no Hospital da Unimed, no bairro da Ilha do Leite, na região central da capital pernambucana.

"Ela vinha lutando contra a doença, passando por vários protocolos, mas não deram os resultados que a equipe médica esperava. Ela foi lutando, mas era uma rotina muito pesada e cansativa e, agora, de fato, ela descansou", disse.

Lucélia e Eduardo estavam juntos havia mais de 20 anos. Os dois se conheceram na Escola Municipal de Frevo do Recife. Professora de artes da prefeitura, ela também atuava como passista no Guerreiros do Passo. Nas apresentações do grupo, a artista interpretava uma personagem caracterizada como uma mulher de época, com vestido listrado.

"Lucélia sempre comigo, em manada, em parceria, companheira, participando das ações do grupo. Ela é professora também, pesquisadora. Ela comigo fundou vários projetos dentro do Guerreiros, projetos de pesquisa. Depois ela se tornou a produtora oficial do grupo, pleiteando recursos em editais públicos para ajudar na manutenção das atividades do grupo", contou.

Lucélia Albuquerque, integrante do grupo de frevo Guerreiros do Passo — Foto: Divulgação/Acervo pessoal

Em maio de 2025, o Guerreiros do Passo ganhou destaque internacional ao participar da estreia do filme "O Agente Secreto", dirigido por Kleber Mendonça Filho e protagonizado por Wagner Moura, durante o Festival de Cannes , na França. O longa conquistou dois prêmios na edição do evento.

O grupo também participou de uma sessão especial do filme no Palácio da Alvorada, em Brasília, a convite do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e da primeira-dama Janja da Silva. A exibição foi chamada de "Cine Alvorada".

"Foi um ano muito bom para o grupo, a gente viajou para a Europa, viajou pelo Brasil. Quando ela chegava, nos intervalos das viagens, de alguma missão, ia para o hospital fazer o tratamento dela. (...) Era uma rotina muito pesada e cansativa", contou.

Segundo Eduardo, a participação nas atividades do grupo ajudava Lucélia a enfrentar o tratamento e, mesmo diante das dificuldades, ela mantinha os planos para o futuro e a disposição de continuar realizando projetos ligados ao frevo.

"A gente ficava ali dentro do universo do frevo, também utilizando essa atuação como uma forma de terapia. Porque, saindo dali, a gente voltava para o hospital fazer tratamento. [...] Ela nunca esmorecia. Tinha uma vontade de viver incrível, uma vontade de fazer as coisas, de realizar. A gente já estava planejando coisas para esse ano que vem. É uma pessoa brilhante, tem uma luz intensa. Sempre foi parceira comigo", declarou.

"Guerreiros do Passo" no Palácio da Alvorada, em Brasília, durante evento para exibição do filme "O Agente Secreto" — Foto: Divulgação/Ricardo Stuckert

A Secretaria de Cultura de Pernambuco (Secult) e a prefeitura do Recife lamentaram a morte de Lucélia e destacaram a contribuição da artista para a preservação e a celebração do frevo, uma das principais expressões da identidade cultural pernambucana.

"Lucélia fez do frevo sua expressão de vida, levando aos corpos, às ruas e à memória coletiva a força, a alegria e a resistência dessa manifestação tão representativa da nossa cultura. Sua dança ajudou a manter viva a tradição e a beleza do frevo, patrimônio cultural de Pernambuco", afirma a nota da Secult.

Já a prefeitura do Recife destacou sua dedicação à salvaguarda da manifestação cultural.

"De hoje em diante, todos os nossos passos voarão ao encontro de Lucélia Albuquerque, passista, atriz, professora, integrante e umas das fundadoras do grupo Guerreiros do Passo, que devotou sua alegria, sua luta de todos os dias e todos os seus voos, até o derradeiro, à salvaguarda e à celebração do frevo", disse.

Eduardo Araújo e Lucélia Albuquerque — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

articles.title: Maestra da própria obra, Marisa Monte rege sinfonia de 'Phonica', show que se conserva perfeito um ano após a estreia | G1
articles.body:
Marisa Monte reapresenta o show 'Phonica' na Brava Arena Jockey, na cidade natal do Rio de Janeiro (RJ) — Foto: Rodrigo Goffredo

♬ Quando Marisa Monte terminou de cantar “Ainda bem” (2011), parceria com Arnaldo Antunes, a artista foi ovacionada pelo público que lotou as pistas e camarotes da Brava Arena Jockey na noite de ontem, sábado, 7 de novembro, para assistir à segunda das três últimas apresentações de “Phonica” no Rio de Janeiro (RJ) na volta do show sinfônico à cidade natal de Marisa, um ano após a chegada do concerto pop ao Rio em 31 de outubro de 2025.

A ovação foi tão grande que cantora e orquestra tiveram que paralisar o show por alguns segundos para Marisa receber os aplausos do público. Situação semelhante aconteceria, sete números depois, quando a cantora terminou de dar voz à apaixonante balada “Depois” (2011), outra parceria de Marisa com Arnaldo e, no caso, também com Carlinhos Brown.

Curiosamente, tanto “Ainda bem” quanto “Depois” são músicas de álbum, “O que você quer saber de verdade” (2011), recebido com certa frieza no lançamento por parte de uma crítica que não soube detectar de imediato a força perene do cancioneiro autoral apresentado por Marisa Monte naquele grande disco...

Em essência, pouco mais de um ano após a estreia nacional da turnê em Belo Horizonte (MG), em 18 de novembro de 2025, “Phonica” se conserva grandioso e perfeito em cena. E, se a orquestra atua sob a batuta certeira do maestro André Bachur, quem rege o concerto e a devoção do público é a própria Marisa Monte , maestra da própria obra e da carreira iniciada em outubro de 1987.

Marisa Monte segue roteiro de 27 músicas na volta do show 'Phonica' ao Rio de Janeiro (RJ) e oferece bônus após o bis — Foto: Rodrigo Goffredo

Ali, no palco da Brava Arena Jockey, estava mais uma vez uma senhora cantora e uma senhora compositora, autora (com parceiros como Arnaldo Antunes, Carlinhos Brown e Nando Reis) de 18 das 27 músicas de um roteiro que, no show de ontem, teve o acréscimo de versão a capella de “Bem que se quis” (“E po' che fà” – Pino Danielle, 1982, em versão em português de Nelson Motta, 1989), bônus que volta e meia Marisa oferece ao público cativo desde o show “Memórias, crônicas e declarações de amor” (2000).

Até os inesperados tropeços da cantora nas letras de “O que você quer saber de verdade” ( Marisa Monte , Arnaldo Antunes e Carlinhos Brown, 2006) e “Infinito particular” ( Marisa Monte , Arnaldo Antunes e Carlinhos Brown, 2006), foram encarados com naturalidade pela maestra, ciente de que ninguém é regente da vida. “A vida é assim. Nada sob controle”, gracejou a artista após o canto de “Infinito particular”.

Prestes a completar 60 anos de vida e 40 de carreira em 2027, efemérides que não deverão passar em branco ao longo do próximo ano, Marisa Monte consegue se impor naturalmente, sem afetação ou ares de superioridade, diante da orquestra comandada por Bachur.

Todo mundo vê e sente que é ela, Marisa, a delicada regente da sinfonia pop de “Phonica” , show que merecia ser perpetuado em registro audiovisual pela beleza do concerto e dos arranjos criados por Ubiratan Marques (maestro da Orquestra Afrosinfônica, da Bahia), o violinista Newton Carneiro e os pianistas Thiago Costa, Débora Gurgel e Jether Garotti para embalar um repertório majoritariamente autoral que reforça a assinatura imprimida por Marisa Monte na música brasileira há 35 anos, precisamente desde 1991, ano em que a cantora começou a gravar as próprias músicas no álbum “Mais” .

Enfim, “Phonica” representa o triunfo dessa obra ora enquadrada em moldura orquestral, em interseção com a linguagem da música erudita, sem diluição do apelo pop.

Marisa Monte e o maestro André Bachur saúdam o público ao fim da apresentação do concerto pop 'Phonica' na Brava Arena Jockey — Foto: Rodrigo Goffredo

articles.title: Festival de Serra de São Bento recebe Vanessa da Mata, Dorgival e SPC | G1
articles.standfirst: Após adiamento, evento comemora 15 anos com programação de quinta-feira (12) a domingo (15), na cidade de Serra de São Bento.
articles.summary: Após adiamento, evento comemora 15 anos com programação de quinta-feira (12) a domingo (15), na cidade de Serra de São Bento.
articles.body:
A edição 2026 do Festival Multicultural de Serra de São Bento será realizado de quinta (12) a domingo (15), com a presença de atrações nacionais como Vanessa da Mata, Dorgival Dantas, Henry Freitas e Só Pra Contrariar. O acesso é gratuito.

O festival celebra 15 anos de existência em 2026 e a expectativa da organização é que a cidade de Serra de São Bento receba mais de 70 mil pessoas ao longo dos quatro dias de programação. Municípios vizinhos também se movimentam para receber visitantes.

A noite de abertura, na quinta-feira (12), será dedicada à música gospel, com o pastor Roberto Pontes, o Ministério de Louvor Sublime Trono e Canção & Louvor.

Dorgival Dantas se apresenta no Festival Multicultural de Serra de São Bento — Foto: Bruna Couto/g1

Vanessa da Mata, Henry Freitas, Raynel Guedes e Mercinho sobem ao palco na sexta-feira (13).

No sábado (14) tem Só Pra Contrariar, Dorgival Dantas e Katia & Aduílio, além da Banda Cítrika.

O encerramento no domingo (15) contará com shows de João Marcos e Banda, César Soanata e Banda Zaya.

"A valorização de talentos locais e de estados vizinhos garante visibilidade a artistas que raramente ocupam palcos de grande porte na região", afirmou Diel Figueiredo, secretário de Turismo de Serra de São Bento.

Além da arena principal dos shows, o Festival terá praça turística com apresentação de mais de 25 bandas regionais, que começam de manhã e vão até as 22h. A feira gastronômica e a exposição de artesanato também integram a programação.

O Festival de Serra de São Bento seria realizado entre 31 de julho e 2 de agosto, mas foi adiado por conta do bloqueio de repasses federais , ocasionado pelas eleições.

articles.title: 'Ramayana' box office collection day 4 (LIVE): The Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi starrer crosses Rs 230 crore net in India, Diwali, Laxmi Puja to play key role in determining Sunday numbers
articles.summary: ‘Ramayana: Part I’, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash among others, has maintained its strong momentum at the Indian box office on its first
articles.body: ‘Ramayana: Part I’, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash among others, has maintained its strong momentum at the Indian box office on its first Sunday. The film released on November 5, Thursday while it dropped on day 2, Friday, the growth on Saturday was quite encouraging. The Sunday numbers further show significant jump over its collections at the same time on each of its previous three days. With day 4 coinciding with Diwali and Lakshmi Puja, the film's evening business could face some pressure as festivities are likely to keep a section of moviegoers occupied.A comparison of its day-wise performance at the corresponding reporting time highlights the film's steady growth. ‘Ramayana’ had collected Rs 64.85 crore net on its day 1. It saw a drop of around 25 percent on day 2, which is Friday bringing its second day total to Rs 48 crore net. On Saturday, it made more than the first day, with Rs 69.80crore. On Sunday, till evening the film has collected Rs 47.83 crore. The total net collection in India now stands at Rs 230.53 crore.Day wise collection of 'Ramayana: Part 1'Day 1 (Thursday) - Rs 64.85 croreDay 2 (Friday) - Rs 48.05 croreDay 3 (Saturday) - Rs 69.80 croreDay 4 (Sunday) LIVE - Rs 47.83 croreTotal net collection in India - Rs 230.53 croreThe Sunday trend comes after the film registered its biggest single-day collection on Saturday, earning Rs. 67.80 crore nett. Its strong start on Day 4 indicates sustained audience interest, although the eventual collection will depend on how well it holds up during the evening.Diwali and Lakshmi Puja could, however, prove to be a key factor in determining the film's final Sunday total. The evening is traditionally reserved for prayers and celebrations, with families attending pujas at home and visiting friends and relatives. This can affect theatrical footfalls even for films enjoying strong audience interest. It remains to be seen whether ‘Ramayana’ can sustain its momentum despite the festive-day challenge.Karnataka and Maharashtra have emerged as the leading contributors to the film's Sunday collections so far, with Bengaluru and Mumbai among its strongest-performing cities.'Ramayana' is directed by Nitesh Tiwari.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Gonzalo Bernardos, economista, critica la huelga general y se enzarza con Afra Blanco: "Por primera vez en el mundo hay una prospectiva"
articles.standfirst: El profesor universitario critica con severidad a los sindicatos
articles.summary: El profesor universitario critica con severidad a los sindicatos
articles.body: El economista Gonzalo Bernardos se ha mostrado muy crítico con la huelga general convocada para este próximo miércoles, 11 de noviembre. El profesor universitario, en 'La Sexta Xplica', ha criticado esta medida de presión social. "Por primera vez en la historia, una asociación que no sabemos quién la financia ni cuánta gente tiene afiliada va a convocar una huelga. Y la huelga es convocada por 'a ver qué sucede'. Es prácticamente para que no venga el Partido Popular porque 'uy lo que va a poder hacer'. Es una huelga prospectiva", ha comentado durante su turno de palabra. Gonzalo Bernardos, por otra parte, ha valorado el papel de los sindicatos: "Han sido muy importantes para generar una mayor igualdad, pero yo estoy decepcionadísimo con los sindicatos. Ya lo estoy desde que apoyaron el derecho a decidir en Cataluña por cobrar las subvenciones de la Generalitat". El economista ha denunciado, según ha explicado, las subvenciones que reciben los sindicatos por parte del gobierno. "Y atención, señores, ¿qué se puede hacer con 155 millones? Es la subvención que se ha dado a las organizaciones sindicales el Ministerio de Trabajo. En 2018 daba 8,8 millones y ahora da 32 millones. Los grandes beneficiados en 2025, UGT y Comisiones Obreras", ha manifestado. Gonzalo Bernardos, tras plantear este dato, ha cuestionado el papel de estas organizaciones: "Los sindicatos, con esta convocatoria de huelga, indiscutiblemente se han desprestigiado. Y quiero dejar muy claro que han hecho mucho, pero que los actuales dirigentes lo que hacen es un desprestigio". Afra Blanco no ha tardado en responder a las palabras del economista catalán: "Se me hinchado lo que ya no suena y lo digo así de claro. Las organizaciones sindicales tienen más afiliados que los partidos políticos. Cachondeos los justos. Lo que está diciendo el señor Bernardos es que un trabajador cuando se vaya directamente a una oferta de empleo, si no está sindicado, se negocio su sueldo, sus vacaciones, sus descansos, sus jornadas, sus planes de igualdad... Esto no pasa porque las negocian las organizaciones sindicales".

articles.title: Pierce Brosnan backs 'Fantastic Beasts' star for next James Bond, predicts fans will be 'blown away'
articles.summary: Pierce Brosnan singled out Callum Turner as a standout among the actors being considered for the next James Bond role in a Vanity Fair interview.
articles.body: Pierce Brosnan is throwing in his two cents into the conversation regarding who should be chosen to play the next James Bond, nearly 25 years after he last played the iconic character. During a recent interview with Vanity Fair, the 73-year-old actor said he is following along with the public as "an audience member," adding he is just as "eager" as everyone else "to see who is going to play this epic role of cinematic history." He did however give one actor a special shout out. "All the men who are on the list now are actors I admire," he said. "Callum, Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong. They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men." While he doesn't know who will take on the iconic role next, Brosnan wishes whoever is chosen "the very best of life and strength and courage." FORMER BOND GIRL SAYS NEXT 007 SHOULD BE 'ANOTHER GORGEOUS MAN' AS JAMES BOND DECISION Brosnan first appeared as agent 007 in the 1995 movie, "GoldenEye," having taken over the reigns from Timothy Dalton. He appeared in his final Bond movie in 2002 with the release of "Die Another Day," and was replaced by Daniel Craig in the 2006 movie, "Casino Royale." Craig starred as James Bond in six films, before hanging up his badge following the release of "No Time to Die" in 2021. "You know, it’s hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond," Brosnan said. In addition to a new actor playing Bond, the film is also getting a new director in Denis Villeneuve, who will be taking over the franchise, which excites Brosnan. His work is visionary, and his stealth and imagination of camera work and storytelling is so visceral and sensuous," he said. "It’s going to be great. It’s going to be truly magnificent." When speaking with GQ about the mental and physical load of playing the character in September 2022, he nonchalantly explained, "You get chipped, you get nicked, you pull muscles, you get stitched up." He also spoke to the outlet about his own approach to playing James Bond, saying he "was trying to walk a line between Roger [Moore] and Sean Connery," who played the role before him, and "not being shy about taking from their work." "I allowed myself the grace to try and get the sense of humour that both men brought to the part," he said. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? articles.title: PSOE y PP usan canciones de Extremoduro para pelearse en X y las redes sociales piden no usar el nombre de Robe Iniesta en política
articles.standfirst: Todo comenzó porque Pedro Sánchez recomendó una canción del grupo liderado por el difunto artista
articles.summary: Todo comenzó porque Pedro Sánchez recomendó una canción del grupo liderado por el difunto artista
articles.body: Los partidos políticos se encuentran sumidos en plena lucha pre elecciones generales, que tienen lugar el próximo 29 de noviembre. PSOE y PP son las dos grandes formaciones que tratarán de formar gobierno, aunque, las últimas encuestas colocan a Vox mucho más cerca de ellos de lo que parece. Pero antes de votar, tienen lugar las campañas electorales. Este domingo, 8 de noviembre, Pedro Sánchez, tras el mitin dado en Bilbao, País Vasco, en el Palacio Euskalduna, usó una canción de Extremoduro para alentar a sus seguidores: “Siempre habrá música”, publicó en X, añadiendo un link de Spotify que redirigía a la canción ‘Ama, ama, ama y ensancha el alma’, de la banda dirigida por el difunto Robe Iniesta. A esto ha contestado el Partido Popular (PP), respondiendo directamente al post: “De Extremoduro también es buena la de ‘So payaso’, Pedro”, incluso algunos de sus seguidores dieron ideas como el tema ‘Puta’. Pero la cosa no quedó aquí, ya que los socialistas contestaron: “No os habéis leído la letra”, fue lo que dijeron, enviándoles la letra completa de la canción en la publicación. Sin embargo, esto no ha gustado a muchos, que no han dudado en pedir que no se use la memoria de Robe, fallecido el pasado 10 de diciembre de 2025, para atacarse entre sí. Uno de los posts anónimos que contestaron a estas publicaciones decía: “Robe Iniesta, el líder de Extremoduro, mantuvo a lo largo de su carrera una postura escéptica y crítica con la política institucional en general, sin casarse con ninguna sigla, incluido el PSOE. El músico siempre defendió su independencia y evitó que los partidos utilizaran su figura o sus canciones con fines partidistas”, recibiendo varios ‘me gusta’. Otro, apuntó: “No entiendo muy bien que, sabiendo que a Robe no le gustaría estar en tuit de ningún partido, hagáis esto, al menos podríais respetar la memoria de los que ya no están”.

articles.title: Bill Murray pours Guinness for fans at New York bar after admitting fame 'is not easy'
articles.summary: Bill Murray played bartender on Halloween night, pouring perfect pints of Guinness for cheering fans at a bar in Yonkers and posing for photos.
articles.body: Bill Murray was spotted enjoying Halloween in Yonkers, New York, where he interacted with fans while working behind the bar. The 76-year-old actor and former "Saturday Night Live" star was photographed sitting with Rory Dolan, the owner of Rory Dolan's Restaurant & Bar, and showing off his bartending skills by pouring Guinness for customers. The actor looked like a natural behind the bar as fans cheered when he poured a glass of Guinness. "He had a bottle of wine, a very nice bottle of wine, and he also had, he was drinking some beer, but he did pour a pint of Guinness," Dolan told Fox News Digital. "Three-part pour, which is good to see him doing it. It wasn't his first time to do it!" ACTOR BILL MURRAY STUNS TRUMP'S TOP ECONOMIC ADVISOR WITH BIZARRE QUESTION ON NEWS SHOW According to Dolan, Murray arrived at the restaurant on his own. Murray kept it casual in a black outfit, with a navy blue button-up vest over a long-sleeved black shirt. In addition to serving drinks, Murray took time to pose for photos with other patrons at the bar. "I think because he really was looking for the Irish culture," Dolan said. "He had been in Ireland doing this show. He has an excellent show out, but he was building on that energy, and he wanted to get behind the bar, pour a pint, and he wanted to know all about me and Rory Dolan's and whatever else. He was just very inquisitive, and he was very, very gracious to all, every one of the customers who went up and asked for photographs and spoke to them at length, and he was just, it was just great to have him." Dolan also shared that the restaurant was celebrating another patron's 90th birthday the night Murray visited. "The 90th birthday was that evening and then the crowd was in before the 90th birthday," Dolan said. "There was a big funeral, and they all came out to the bar, and it was just, the place was full and he was loving it." Dolan said other celebrities, including Pierce Brosnan, have also visited the bar. Murray got his big break when he was cast on "Saturday Night Live" in 1977, winning an Emmy for his work on the show's writing staff. He went on to receive an Academy Award nomination, seven Golden Globe nominations with one win, four Emmy nominations with two wins and a BAFTA Award. In his new docuseries, "A Course Called Ireland," Murray discussed his relationship to fame and whether being a public figure makes him happy, answering, "In a word, no." "It's not easy," he said, according to People. "I go through new revelations all the time about how I handle it and how to deal with it. It's not for everyone, but it has also brought me to this place, you know." Despite it not being easy, Murray also admitted that being recognized in public has brought him joy on occasion, most notably when fans share with him how much one of his films means to them. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Meeting fans over the years has helped the "Lost in Translation" star realize there is "a lot of goodwill out there," although he also admitted that he's "not very pleasant." "I think kind of famous people, they can decide that there's a certain way to play being famous, you know?" he said. When asked how he handles fame, Murray said, "Well, I’m not very pleasant. You can see that. I think just being nice-nice, I don’t go for nice-nice. If I were like an ordinary citizen acting the way that I do, I’d probably have a lot more cuts and bruises." The "Ghostbusters" star most recently starred in the six-part docuseries, "A Course Called Ireland," which is inspired by the book of the same name. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS The series follows Murray and author Tom Coyne as they travel throughout Ireland while playing golf on legendary courses and meeting members of Murray's family, as well as local celebrities. "Well, it sounded like it was going to be a piece of cake," he told The Irish Examiner in October about why he agreed to the show. "We’d have to go over to Ireland, talk to bartenders, play beautiful golf courses, eat beautiful food, and roll around through a beautiful country. It sounded like a beautiful, beautiful idea. It was the beauty. I’m a sucker for beauty. That’s all." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "A Course Called Ireland" is available to stream on Paramount+. articles.title: SNL has a new impression of Elon Musk, ‘the worst thing South Africa has ever done’
articles.summary: SNL seems to have its knives out for tech executives.
articles.body:
Saturday Night Live cast member Jeremy Culhane unveiled his impression of Elon Musk last night, depicting the SpaceX and Tesla CEO as an awkward loser who fumbles his attempt to befriend the hosts of Weekend Update.

This isn’t the first time the show has lampooned the world’s richest man ( and one-time SNL host ), with Mike Myers dropping by occasionally to wield a chainsaw before freezing and muttering, “Glitch!”

Since Musk was in the news this week for spending half a billion dollars on candidates who lost in the midterms , then announcing plans to halt Cybertruck production , it’s maybe not surprising that Culhane’s version is a little less obnoxious and a little more desperate to be liked, doing his best to laugh off his setbacks and remind the audience, “ My car did a flip !”

Eventually, Weekend Update co-host Colin Jost asks a pointed question about Musk’s week: “You moved to Texas because California was run by Democrats. You moved all your companies to Texas because you didn’t want to pay taxes. You even built your own town in Texas. And now Texas is run by Democrats. Now you’re going to have to pay taxes. So how does that make you feel?”

Culhane nods along with each step of the question, then answers, “Bad?”

To show that he’s a good sport about all this, Culhane also asks his chatbot Grok to do “an epic vulgar roast of me, Elon Musk.” Grok delivers, describing Musk as “the worst thing South Africa has ever done” and suggesting, “Maybe if you have 100 more kids, one of them will talk to you .”

This week’s episode also featured a spoof of the Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything,” featuring Jane Wickline’s uncanny take on the Theranos founder (though most of the jokes focus on episode host Druski).

SNL seems to have its knives out for tech executives this season, starting with Wickline’s impression of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei as a stuttering prophet of AI doom.

A couple weeks later, James Austin Johnson caricatured data center backer/”Marty Supreme” co-star Kevin O’Leary . Asked about the widespread public opposition to data centers, Johnson-as-O’Leary smoothly replies, “All I want is to buy up 40,000 acres of God’s untouched splendor and replace it with a very loud computer that steals your job.”

articles.title: 'American Idol' star Justin Guarini endured dark spiral after Hollywood dream collapsed
articles.summary: "American Idol" alum Justin Guarini opens up about the dark spiral after RCA dropped him and how embracing failure led to Broadway, "Wicked" and a whole new identity.
articles.body: At the start of his career, Justin Guarini seemed to have it all: fame, fortune and a promising future in Hollywood. After becoming the runner-up on the first season of "American Idol" in 2002, Guarini was thrust into the spotlight seemingly overnight. But when his Hollywood dream came crashing down, he found himself in a dark place that he would eventually come to view as one of his greatest blessings. "I think it was one of the greatest things that could ever have happened to me," Guarini, who recently released his book, "Center Stage Confidence: How to Own Your Story and Command Any Room," told Fox News Digital. "Failure is the greatest teacher, one of the greatest teachers that we can have in any given situation because in that failure, you have one of two paths. You either give up or you keep going." TAYLOR HICKS CREDITS FAITH AND BLUE-COLLAR BIRMINGHAM ROOTS FOR KEEPING HIM GROUNDED AFTER 'AMERICAN IDOL' WIN However, this mindset didn't sink in until much later. In his book, Guarini recalled the moment he learned he had been dropped by his record label, RCA, in 2003. "I stared at the TV in shock as my entire world came crumbling down around my ears," Guarini, who said he learned the news during a "Weekend Update" segment on "Saturday Night Live," wrote in his book. "Every illusion of fame, fortune, and glory fell away in an instant — only to be replaced by the silence of loss. In that moment, the veil of my arrogance, my assumptions, and my entitlement were lifted away, and I saw my life for what it had become." "I lost weight, slept more and more, and became less and less like myself, and the people who loved me started to notice and worry. I was living the ghost of the life I had always dreamed of and burning money and time in equal and absurd measure." 'GOLDBERGS’ STAR JEFF GARLIN SAYS HE PLANNED TO TAKE HIS OWN LIFE AMID TURBULENT FINAL DAYS ON SITCOM As the first runner-up in "Idol" history, Guarini believed his future in the entertainment industry was secure. But his early success proved difficult to sustain. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE In 2003, he released his self-titled debut album and starred alongside Kelly Clarkson in the musical romantic comedy "From Justin to Kelly." While his album debuted in the top 20 on the Billboard 200 chart, the movie flopped, and criticism of his performance and appearance continued. WATCH: 'AMERICAN IDOL' STAR JUSTIN GUARINI ENDURED DARK SPIRAL AFTER HOLLYWOOD DREAM COLLAPSED As his career stalled, Guarini struggled to reconcile his newfound reality with the life he had envisioned. KELLY CLARKSON WON’T LET HER KIDS WATCH ‘FROM JUSTIN TO KELLY’ AFTER BRUTAL ADMISSION ABOUT 2003 FILM "There have been plenty of people who've given up and failed and found other things," Guarini told Fox News Digital. "That's really wonderful. But for me, that dark place of not wanting to get out of bed, not wanting to look at myself in the mirror, not wanting to go out and see anything, it just was a period of isolation. And it's very easy to do when you live behind a gate in an exclusive community." Over time, Guarini began to change his outlook. COUNTRY STAR GABBY BARRETT SAYS SHE 'SLEPT IN THE CAR' BEFORE 'AMERICAN IDOL' CHANGED HER LIFE "I realized that there were still people celebrating me," he said. "I realized there was still something worth celebrating in my life. And it wasn't the vanity metrics of how many people voted for me or how many followers I would end up having or the amount of money I could make or blah, blah. It was just doing something and going back to something that I really truly loved." For Guarini, that meant returning to the stage. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "For me, that came in the form of just going back out and getting on the stage and singing for people. And I would do it at everything from gala events to state fairs to wherever." Those smaller performances eventually paved the way for a new chapter in his career. After independently releasing his second album in 2005, Guarini found opportunities in television before making his Broadway debut in "Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown" in 2010. He went on to appear in several Broadway productions, including "American Idiot," "Romeo and Juliet" and "Wicked." In 2015, he introduced audiences to another side of his talent when he began portraying Lil' Sweet, the flamboyant character featured in Diet Dr Pepper advertising campaigns. Looking back, Guarini said his willingness to embrace failure rather than run from it ultimately led to opportunities he might never have experienced had his initial fame endured. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "So there was a cascading effect. So the bottom line was being willing to sit in that place of failure, of discontent, darkness, but continue to go and continue to just say, ‘Okay, how can I continue to move through this space of discomfort, learn about myself and keep going?’ And ultimately, that led to a massive amount of growth that I don't think would have happened had I just, you know, stayed famous." Now, nearly 25 years after his "Idol" debut, Guarini said his successes and failures have taught him one thing: don't give up. "And so, for me, it has been almost 25 years now of some awesome ups and downs, and every single time I go up and down and up and down, it's just a consistency again of staying in the game," he said. This life in this world is cyclical and if you stay in the game, and you do good work, and you're kind to people, the opportunity always comes back around to you, and you'll be more prepared to take advantage of it when it does," he added.

articles.title: Alanis Morissette identifies as pansexual, months after reflecting on Sarah Jessica Parker 'SATC' kiss
articles.summary: Alanis Morissette revealed she is pansexual on the "Handsome" podcast, joking she likes to "confuse people on the way out" with such revelations.
articles.body: Alanis Morissette’s recent decision to publicly identify as pansexual has cast her famous same-sex kiss with Sarah Jessica Parker on "Sex and the City" in a new light. The singer, 52, opened up about her sexuality during an appearance on the "Handsome" podcast after previously discussing the memorable 2000 scene on Alex Cooper’s "Call Her Daddy" podcast in September. Morissette appeared on "Sex and the City" in the season 3 episode "Boy, Girl, Boy, Girl…" as Dawn, a woman who kisses Parker’s character, Carrie Bradshaw, during a game of spin the bottle. ALANIS MORISSETTE SAYS WEBSITES WERE BUILT TO PLOT HER MURDER AFTER 'JAGGED LITTLE PILL' SUCCESS During her September appearance on "Call Her Daddy," Morissette revealed that she helped pitch the storyline to the show’s producers. "I reached out to them and I said, ‘Might it be a nice time for Carrie to experience a lesbian moment?’" Morissette said. "And they said, ‘Why, yes. We were thinking the same thing.’" GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "I think we literally had the same idea at the same time," she added. "That happens." Morissette also reflected on the kiss itself, describing the moment with Parker as "easy" and "buoyant." "I do recall kissing her," she said. "It was very pleasant." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Morissette’s comments resurfaced after she publicly identified as pansexual during Tuesday’s episode of the "Handsome" podcast, co-hosted by Tig Notaro, Fortune Feimster and Mae Martin. The conversation turned to the singer’s rocky dating history with men. "I’m sorry for the men that hurt you, but I’m not sorry for the songs that came from it," Feimster told Morissette before asking, "Did it make you want to be a lesbian at any point?" "I’m pansexual, so, yeah," Morissette replied. "Wait, you’re not really pansexual, are you?" Notaro asked. "I am," Morissette confirmed. "You’re supposed to come into the ‘Handsome’ podcast leading with, ‘I’m pansexual,’" Notaro said. "You know, I like to leave it for the epilogue," Morissette responded. "I like to confuse people on the way out." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Morissette previously spoke about sexuality during a 2008 interview with The Advocate. "I think it’s a beautiful rite of passage for everyone to play with their sexuality at some point, so I did exactly that," she said. "And it was great!" "I’ve felt love from the gay community since I was really young because all my friends were gay," Morissette added. "There’s a passion, a presence, and a curiosity with a lot of gay people that I meet, and that aliveness is such a special quality to me." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

articles.title: Chynna Phillips admits she considered calling lawyer to end Billy Baldwin marriage after 'treacherous times'
articles.summary: Chynna Phillips admits she considered calling a lawyer to end her marriage to Billy Baldwin, but his willingness to work on their decades-long marriage changed everything.
articles.body: Chynna Phillips and Billy Baldwin's marriage has weathered some difficult moments, including a time when the singer considered ending their relationship. The Wilson Phillips singer, who has been married to the actor for more than three decades, opened up about the challenges they've faced during an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital at the Chiller Theatre Expo in New Jersey. "Billy and I have had some really treacherous times in our marriage, and there were times when I was going to throw in the towel and call a lawyer," Phillips said. KIMBERLY WILLIAMS-PAISLEY CREDITS TWO-WORD PHRASE AS THE SECRET BEHIND HER 23-YEAR MARRIAGE TO BRAD PAISLEY "If we're being completely transparent here, there were times where I was just thinking to myself, I can't do this anymore." WATCH: CHYNNA PHILLIPS OPENS UP ABOUT NEARLY ENDING MARRIAGE TO BILLY BALDWIN: 'TREACHEROUS TIMES' Despite reaching that breaking point, Phillips said her husband's willingness to work on their relationship gave her hope that things could improve. "But then when I saw that he was actually willing to work on the relationship in a very intentional way, the two of us were able to make some changes that were permanent," she said. Phillips explained that the couple began making lasting changes rather than falling back into the same patterns after a brief period of improvement. WILLIE ROBERTSON'S FAITH-BASED ADVICE THAT'S KEPT HIS 34-YEAR MARRIAGE TO WIFE KORIE STRONG "We have been working very, very hard," she said. Phillips and Baldwin tied the knot in September 1995 and share three adult children, Jameson, Vance and Brooke. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Their marriage has made headlines in recent years as the couple has spoken publicly about their decision to live separately at different points in their relationship. In October, Phillips confirmed that she and Baldwin had moved into separate houses while continuing to work through their marital challenges. "Literally our marriage was going down like the Titanic, and Billy moved 50 yards away from me in the guest house and so far, so good," Phillips said in an Instagram video. "It's kind of working. I'm not really sure what's going to come of it but hey, I'm not fighting it." View this post on Instagram A post shared by Chynna Phillips Baldwin (@chynna_phillips) The couple previously lived apart in 2024, with Phillips staying in Santa Barbara and Baldwin living in Beverly Hills. They later reunited under one roof before deciding to live separately again. Now, Phillips and Baldwin are preparing to give fans a closer look at their relationship through a new YouTube series, "Holding On: Billy and Chynna," scheduled to debut Nov. 17. During her interview with Fox News Digital, Phillips encouraged viewers to check out the project, which she said offers an unfiltered look at the realities of marriage. "It really depicts marriage, the ups, the downs, it's very raw, it's very real, it is very funny, and it's super engaging in my opinion," she said. "I'm a little biased, but..." MARCUS MUMFORD SAYS BIBLE CAMP SPARKED DECADES-LONG LOVE STORY WITH WIFE CAREY MULLIGAN In a teaser shared on Instagram, Baldwin and Phillips were seen discussing some of the tensions in their relationship. "You can't admit when you're wrong. That's just it," Baldwin told his wife in the preview. "You can't either!" Phillips responded. In another clip, Baldwin said Phillips had told him she wanted to spend her life with him, but wanted to spend it "adjacent." While Phillips has been candid about the challenges in her marriage, family remains an important part of her life. WATCH: CHYNNA PHILLIPS SAYS BOND WITH FAMOUS SISTERS IS STRONGER THAN EVER: 'NOW WE'RE INSEPARABLE' The singer also reflected on her evolving relationship with her sisters, Mackenzie and Bijou Phillips, during her conversation with Fox News Digital. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "It's interesting because we didn't grow up together," Phillips said. "Bijou and Mackenzie spent a lot more time together than I did with them. I was basically raised as an only child, but as I matured and grew older, I reached out more to them, and we all started spending more time together and now we're inseparable." Phillips, whose father was the late musician John Phillips of The Mamas & the Papas, said the sisters have developed a strong bond despite their different childhood experiences. "We spend a whole lot of time together, and we trust each other implicitly," she said. "Of course, we've had our ups and our downs just like any siblings. But we really love one another and I think that we share, since we share the same father, there's just a very strong connection between us." WATCH: Chynna Phillips embraces California roots and family life: 'I'm a California girl' Faith has also played a significant role in Phillips' life, although she said she doesn't frequently discuss her beliefs with her sisters. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "I don't really talk about my faith too much with my sisters, but they know that I love the Lord," she said. "So I just kind of pray for them, and I know that they're in the Jesus waiting room." These days, Phillips said she enjoys a quieter lifestyle in Santa Barbara, where she spends time cooking, taking walks and relaxing at home. With her three children now grown, she also finds joy in caring for her two dogs, Hula and Hoops. "I just love being at home and cooking. And I love taking long naps and walks and hanging out with Billy," she said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
